wrong: If I lived closer to work, I'd cycle every day.
What would you do if you lost your job?
If she were here, she would know what to do.
The deal would certainly have been signed.
The deal was impossible from the start.
The deal was signed in the end.
If you had called me, I would have picked you up.
We could have saved money if we had booked earlier.
If it hadn't rained, the concert wouldn't have been cancelled.
If you told us earlier, we could have adjusted the schedule.
If you had told us earlier, we could have adjust the schedule.
If you would tell us earlier, we could have adjusted the schedule.

ct-B22-2a.correct: A is about the past, B about now or the future.
wrong: A is about now, B about the past.
A is about the future, B the past.
There is no difference in meaning.
ct-B22-2a.why: Third conditional (A) = an unreal past. Second conditional (B) = an unreal present or future.
ct-B22-2a.why_lv: Third conditional (A) izsaka nereālu pagātni. Second conditional (B) izsaka nereālu tagadni vai nākotni.

wrong: Had we checked the forecast, we wouldn't have gone sailing.
If she'd asked me, I'd have helped her.
They wouldn't have got lost if they had taken a map.
If I realised the impact of my decision, I would have acted differently.
If I would have realised the impact of my decision, I would have acted differently.
If I hadn't missed the train, I'd be at home by now.
If she had saved more, she wouldn't be worried about money now.
We'd know the results now if they had sent the email.
If I didn't stay up so late, I wouldn't have been so tired now.
If I hadn't stayed up so late, I wouldn't have been so tired now.
If I wouldn't have stayed up so late, I wouldn't be so tired now.

answers: If he had taken the job, he would be living in Paris now.
If he'd taken the job, he'd be living in Paris now.
He would be living in Paris now if he had taken the job.
He'd be living in Paris now if he'd taken the job.
If he had taken the job, he would live in Paris now.
If he'd taken the job, he'd live in Paris now.
He would live in Paris now if he had taken the job.
If he had taken the job, he would be in Paris now.
If he'd taken the job, he'd be in Paris now.
He would be in Paris now if he had taken the job.
If he had taken the job, he might be living in Paris now.
If he'd taken the job, he might be living in Paris now.

wrong: If she spoke French, she would have got the job in Paris.
If I hadn't eaten so much, I wouldn't feel sick now.
If he weren't so shy, he would have asked her to dance.

cm-B22-5a.q: A colleague says: 'If I had a better memory, I would have remembered your birthday.' What does the sentence say?
cm-B22-5a.correct: The colleague's memory is poor, and that is why they forgot your birthday.
wrong: The colleague's memory was poor in the past, but it is fine now.
The colleague remembered your birthday.
The colleague will remember your birthday next year.
cm-B22-5a.why: The if-part is past simple: a quality now (the colleague's memory is poor). The result is *would have* + past participle: the past (the birthday was forgotten). The poor memory is the reason.
cm-B22-5a.why_lv: *If* daļā ir Past Simple: īpašība tagad (kolēģim ir slikta atmiņa). Otrajā daļā ir *would have* + 3. forma: pagātne (dzimšanas diena tika aizmirsta). Slikta atmiņa ir iemesls.

cm-C11-3a.q: Say it in a more formal way, without *if*: If I had listened to my accountant, I wouldn't be in this mess now.

wrong: Had she known, she would have stayed.
Had the train been on time, we would be home by now.
Were I braver, I would have said no.
He said he was working from home.
They told us the shop was closed.
She told me she had lost her keys.
She asked if I wanted a coffee.
They asked where we had parked the car.
He wanted to know how long the trip would take.
He asked me if I was ready.
They asked whether we had eaten.
He wanted to know whether the hotel had a pool.
He denied taking the money.
My doctor advised me to rest.
They promised that they would call back.

rv-C11-4a.correct: My manager accused me for losing the file.
wrong: She apologised for being late.
He insisted on paying for dinner.
They congratulated us on our new home.
rv-C11-4a.why: *accuse* + person + *of* + -ing: *My manager accused me of losing the file.*
rv-C11-4a.why_lv: *accuse* + persona + *of* + darbības vārds ar -ing: *My manager accused me of losing the file.*

ia-B22-4a.correct: We still can't decide whether moving to a bigger flat.
wrong: I don't know what to say to him.
Why the meeting was cancelled is still a mystery.
Do you know whether the museum is open on Mondays?
ia-B22-4a.why: After *whether* use *to* + base verb or a full clause: *whether to move* or *whether we should move* to a bigger flat.
ia-B22-4a.why_lv: Aiz *whether* lieto *to* + pamatforma vai pilnu palīgteikumu: *whether to move* vai *whether we should move* to a bigger flat.

wrong: if
that
what

ia-C11-4a.correct: We talked about how could we cut costs.
wrong: I'm not sure where to park.
Whether the shop is open on Sunday is still unclear.
It depends on whether the flight is on time.
ia-C11-4a.why: No question order after *about*: *how we could cut costs* (or *how to cut costs*).
ia-C11-4a.why_lv: Aiz *about* nav jautājuma vārdu secības: *how we could cut costs* (vai *how to cut costs*).

ia-C12-1a.q: Choose the correct word: ___ booked the meeting room should cancel it if plans change.
wrong: Whomever
Whatever
Wherever
ia-C12-1a.why: *Whoever* is the subject of *booked*. It means *the person who*.
ia-C12-1a.why_lv: *Whoever* ir teikuma priekšmets darbības vārdam *booked*. Tas nozīmē *tas, kurš*.

wrong: Whatever you decide, I'll support you.
You can sit wherever you like.
I'll talk to whoever is at the front desk.
ia-C12-4a.why: *Whoever wins*: *whoever* is the subject of *wins*, so *whomever* is wrong here.
ia-C12-4a.why_lv: *Whoever wins*: *whoever* ir teikuma priekšmets darbības vārdam *wins*, tāpēc *whomever* šeit nav pareizi.

wrong: I wish I had chosen a different course at university.
If only I had a bit more free time now.
If only you had told me about it earlier.

ca-C12-5a.correct: If only we had listened to the warning signs last year, we would not be in this position now.
wrong: If only we would have listened to the warning signs last year, we would not be in this position now.
If only we listened to the warning signs last year, we would not be in this position now.
ca-C12-5a.why: *If only* + *had* + 3rd form for a regret about the past (*last year*), then *would* + base form for the result now. Not *would have listened*, and not *listened*, which is about now.
ca-C12-5a.why_lv: *If only* + *had* + 3. forma izsaka nožēlu par pagātni (*last year*), tad *would* + pamatforma rezultātam tagad. Nav pareizi *would have listened*, un arī *listened*, kas attiecas uz tagadni.

wrong: He asked me what should he do.
He asked me what he does.
She asked me where should she park.
She asked me where she should to park.

answers: whether or not the data was accurate
whether or not the data were accurate

rv-B22-1a.correct: The driver apologised for blocking the exit.
wrong: The driver apologised to block the exit.
The driver apologised of blocking the exit.
The driver apologised blocking the exit.

answers: to me for forgetting the meeting
to me for forgetting about the meeting
for having forgotten about the meeting
to me for having forgotten the meeting
to me for having forgotten about the meeting

rv-C11-1a.q: Which sentence reports this: 'You broke the printer!'

wrong: The manager apologised the delay and promised that it would not happen again.
The manager apologised for the delay and promised it not to happen again.
She suggested me to take the earlier train.
She insisted me to take the earlier train.
She advised to take the earlier train.

rv-C12-5a.q: Which sentence reports the customer's words: 'The service was terrible.'
wrong: The customer complained that the service has been terrible.
The customer complained me that the service was terrible.

ia-B22-1a.q: Which is correct? 'The instructions don't explain ___ the new printer.'
wrong: how should we set up
how set up
ia-B22-1a.why: Question word + *to* + base verb: *how to set up*.
ia-B22-1a.why_lv: Jautājuma vārds + *to* + pamatforma: *how to set up*.

wrong: It remains unclear who is the responsible for the delay.
It remains unclear who responsible is for the delay.

answers: It's not clear who made the decision.
It is not clear who made the decision.
Who made the decision is not clear.
It's unclear who made the decision.
It is unclear who made the decision.
It remains unclear who made the decision.
Who made the decision is unclear.

ia-C11-5a.q: Choose the correct option: The question is ___.

ia-C12-3a.q: Make it one sentence that starts with *Who…*: It doesn't matter who calls. Don't answer.
ia-C12-3a.why: *Whoever* + verb = it does not matter who: *Whoever calls, don't answer.* *Who calls doesn't matter, so don't answer* (the question as the subject) is correct too.
ia-C12-3a.why_lv: *Whoever* + darbības vārds = nav svarīgi, kas: *Whoever calls, don't answer.* Arī *Who calls doesn't matter, so don't answer* ir pareizi (jautājums kā teikuma priekšmets).
answers: Whoever it is, do not answer.
Who calls doesn't matter, so don't answer.
Who calls does not matter, so do not answer.
Whoever may call, do not answer.
Who calls doesn't matter; don't answer.
Who calls does not matter; do not answer.

wrong: By the time the taxi came, we had finished dinner.
I had never tried sushi before that trip.
He told me that he had lost his keys.
Whenever I forget my umbrella, it rains.
If the printer jams, everybody panics.
If you press this button, the machine stops.
If she had more time, she would learn Italian.
What would you do if you saw a ghost?
If I were you, I wouldn't do that.

rq-B12-2a.q: Which sentence reports this question: 'Do you like jazz?'
rq-B12-2a.correct: He asked me if I liked jazz.
wrong: He asked me do I like jazz.
He asked me if did I like jazz.
rq-B12-2a.why: A question without a question word is reported with *if* (or *whether*) and statement word order, no *do / did*: *He asked me if I liked jazz.*
rq-B12-2a.why_lv: Jautājumu bez jautājamā vārda netiešajā runā ievada ar *if* (vai *whether*), vārdu secība ir kā apgalvojumā, bez *do / did*: *He asked me if I liked jazz.*

rq-B12-4a.correct: The receptionist asked me how long would I stay.
wrong: He asked if I wanted a coffee.
She asked whether it was true.
She wanted to know what time the shop closed.
rq-B12-4a.why: A reported question has statement word order: *how long I would stay*, not *how long would I stay*.
rq-B12-4a.why_lv: Netiešajam jautājumam ir apgalvojuma vārdu secība: *how long I would stay*, nevis *how long would I stay*.

wrong: I'm wanting a coffee.
I am want a coffee.
ps-B11-5a.why: *want* is a state verb, so it stays simple: *I want a coffee.*
ps-B11-5a.why_lv: *want* ir stāvokļa darbības vārds, tāpēc paliek Present Simple: *I want a coffee.*

pa-B11-2a.q: Choose the correct option: Yesterday she ___ the door and walked in.
wrong: was opening
has opened
opens
pa-B11-2a.why: A series of finished actions in the past (*yesterday*): past simple: *Yesterday she opened the door and walked in.*
pa-B11-2a.why_lv: Pabeigtu darbību virkne pagātnē (*yesterday*): Past Simple: *Yesterday she opened the door and walked in.*

wrong: since
already
pp-B11-1a.why: *for* + a period of time: *I've worked here for five years.* *since* + a starting point (*since 2020*). *already* does not go before a period of time.
pp-B11-1a.why_lv: *for* + laika posms: *I've worked here for five years.* *since* + sākuma brīdis (*since 2020*). *already* nelieto pirms laika posma.

cf-B11-1a.q: Choose the correct option: We won't finish on time ___ we start now.
wrong: if
when
cf-B11-1a.why: *Unless* = *if ... not*: *We won't finish on time unless we start now* (= if we don't start now).
cf-B11-1a.why_lv: *Unless* = *if ... not*: *We won't finish on time unless we start now* (= ja nesāksim tūlīt).

wrong: She would travel more if she didn't have a dog.
What would you say if your boss offered you a promotion?
If we had a garden, we could grow vegetables.

ct-B12-4a.correct: If I would have seen the message, I would have replied.
wrong: If it hadn't rained, we would have eaten outside.
She wouldn't have got lost if she had taken a map.
What would you have done if the bank had said no?
ct-B12-4a.why: Do not use *would* in the if-part: *If I had seen the message, I would have replied.*
ct-B12-4a.why_lv: *If* daļā nelieto *would*: *If I had seen the message, I would have replied.*

rs-B11-4a.correct: She said me that the meeting was cancelled.
wrong: He told us he had found a new job.
They said they would call back later.
Anna told me she was moving abroad.
rs-B11-4a.why: After *said* we do not put a person directly: *She told me that the meeting was cancelled* or *She said to me that ...*
rs-B11-4a.why_lv: Pēc *said* personu tieši nelieto: *She told me that the meeting was cancelled* vai *She said to me that ...*

wrong: She has lived here since 2015.
He has just left the office.
Have you finished yet?
pp-B11-4a.why: *In 2019* is a finished time, so use the past simple: *We visited Rome in 2019.*
pp-B11-4a.why_lv: *In 2019* ir pabeigts laiks, tāpēc lieto Past Simple: *We visited Rome in 2019.*

pp-B12-2a.q: Choose the correct option: Have you seen the new Italian film? Yes, I ___ it at the cinema last night.
wrong: have seen
have saw
had seen
pp-B12-2a.why: The question asks about experience, but the answer gives a finished time (*last night*): *I saw it at the cinema last night.*
pp-B12-2a.why_lv: Jautājums ir par pieredzi, bet atbildē ir pabeigts laiks (*last night*): *I saw it at the cinema last night.*

ppc-B11-1a.q: Choose the correct option: I'm tired and I'm still at my desk. I ___ all day.
wrong: have been work
have working
had been working

ppf-B12-1a.q: Choose the correct option: The bus left at 8.00. We got to the stop at 8.05. When we got there, the bus ___ already ___.
wrong: has ... left
was ... leaving
did ... leave
ppf-B12-1a.why: The bus left before we got there, so the earlier action is past perfect: *the bus had already left.*
ppf-B12-1a.why_lv: Autobuss aizbrauca pirms mēs atnācām, tāpēc agrākajai darbībai lieto Past Perfect: *the bus had already left.*

fu-B12-1a.q: Choose the correct option: Hurry up! The film ___ start.
wrong: will to
about to
is about
fu-B12-1a.why: *Be about to* + base verb = very soon: *The film is about to start.*
fu-B12-1a.why_lv: *Be about to* + pamatforma = pavisam drīz: *The film is about to start.*

pcp-B12-1a.q: Choose the correct option: The new bridge ___ at the moment.

wrong: The guard told me wait there.
The guard told me waiting there.
The guard asked if I wait there.

ip-B11-1a.correct: Could you tell me when the next train leaves?
wrong: Could you tell me when does the next train leave?
Could you tell me when leaves the next train?
Could you tell me when the next train leave?
ip-B11-1a.why: After *Could you tell me* there is no *does*, and the verb gets its *-s* back: *when the next train leaves.*
ip-B11-1a.why_lv: Pēc *Could you tell me* nelieto *does*, un darbības vārds atkal saņem *-s*: *when the next train leaves.*

wrong: I live with my parents.
Both sound the same.
Both sound permanent.
pc-B11-5a.why: *I'm living with my parents* sounds temporary (for now, not for ever). *I live with my parents* sounds permanent.
pc-B11-5a.why_lv: *I'm living with my parents* izklausās pēc pagaidu situācijas (pagaidām, ne uz visiem laikiem). *I live with my parents* izklausās pastāvīgi.

pp-B12-5a.q: Choose the correct option: I ___ the email yesterday, but the client hasn't answered yet.
wrong: have sent
have just sent
pp-B12-5a.why: *Yesterday* is a finished time, so it needs the past simple: *I sent the email yesterday*. *Hasn't answered yet* is the present perfect: the situation now.
pp-B12-5a.why_lv: *Yesterday* ir pabeigts laiks, tāpēc vajag Past Simple: *I sent the email yesterday*. *Hasn't answered yet* ir Present Perfect: situācija tagad.

psp-B11-5a.q: Choose the correct option: The invoices ___ every Friday, so please send me yours by Thursday.
wrong: are send
send
psp-B11-5a.why: The invoices do not send themselves: someone sends them. So we use *are* + 3rd form: *The invoices are sent every Friday*.
psp-B11-5a.why_lv: Rēķini paši sevi nesūta: tos kāds nosūta. Tāpēc lieto *are* + 3. forma: *The invoices are sent every Friday*.

cf-B11-5a.q: Choose the correct option: If Tom ___ his password again, he'll be locked out of his account.
wrong: will forget
forget
cf-B11-5a.why: After *if* we use the present simple, also for the future, with *-s* after *he*: *If Tom forgets his password again, he'll be locked out*.
cf-B11-5a.why_lv: Pēc *if* lieto Present Simple arī nākotnei, ar *-s* aiz *he*: *If Tom forgets his password again, he'll be locked out*.

pac-B11-1a.q: Choose the correct option: I ___ along the street when I saw an old friend.
wrong: was walk
am walking
were walking
pac-B11-1a.why: The walk was already going on when I saw my friend: *I was walking along the street when I saw an old friend.* The short action (*saw*) interrupts it.
pac-B11-1a.why_lv: Pastaiga jau notika, kad ieraudzīju draugu: *I was walking along the street when I saw an old friend.* Īsā darbība (*saw*) to pārtrauc.

wrong: I waited for an hour last week, then left.
I wait for an hour every day.
I waited an hour, but that was years ago.
The project have been finished.
The project has being finished.
The project is being finished.
ppp-B11-2a.why: *has been* + 3rd form: *The project has been finished.* *Project* is singular, so *has*; and *been*, not *being*.
ppp-B11-2a.why_lv: *has been* + 3. forma: *The project has been finished.* *Project* ir vienskaitlī, tāpēc *has*; un *been*, nevis *being*.

fup-B11-5a.correct: The files will be checked on Monday.
wrong: The files will checked on Monday.
The files will be check on Monday.
The files check on Monday.
fup-B11-5a.why: *will be* + 3rd form: *The files will be checked on Monday.* We do not say who checks them.
fup-B11-5a.why_lv: *will be* + 3. forma: *The files will be checked on Monday.* Mēs nesakām, kas tos pārbaudīs.

wrong: We booked early.
We will book early.
We got a cheaper flight.

pac-B12-4a.correct: We are going to stay longer last summer, but the hotel was full.
wrong: I was going to call you, but I lost your number.
She was going to leave when he arrived.
They were going to meet us, but their train was late.
pac-B12-4a.why: A plan in the past needs *was / were going to*; *are going to* is for plans now: *We were going to stay longer last summer, but the hotel was full.*
pac-B12-4a.why_lv: Plānam pagātnē vajag *was / were going to*; *are going to* lieto tagadnes plāniem: *We were going to stay longer last summer, but the hotel was full.*

wrong: She is running.
She runs.
ppc-B11-5a.why: She stopped running a moment ago and we can see the result now: *She has been running.* *She is running* would mean she is still running.
ppc-B11-5a.why_lv: Viņa nupat beidza skriet, un rezultāts ir redzams tagad: *She has been running.* *She is running* nozīmētu, ka viņa joprojām skrien.

ppc-B12-3a.q: The children are washing their hands now. Look at the floor! They ___ with paint. (play)
ppc-B12-3a.why: They have stopped, but the floor shows what they were doing: *They have been playing with paint.*
ppc-B12-3a.why_lv: Viņi ir beiguši, bet grīda rāda, ko viņi darīja: *They have been playing with paint.*

fu-B12-4a.correct: My sister going to start a new job next month.
fu-B12-4a.why: *Going to* needs *am / is / are* before it: *My sister is going to start a new job next month.*
fu-B12-4a.why_lv: Pirms *going to* vajag *am / is / are*: *My sister is going to start a new job next month.*

fu-B12-6a.q: The sky is full of dark clouds, and your friend has no umbrella. Write two sentences to your friend: what you expect to happen, and an offer of your umbrella.
